title: Resolve Rig Kontrol switch 2 and 9 mapping
description: Switches 2 and 9 must be resolved before the live MIDI bridge work continues. Existing evidence is inconclusive: focused capture saw mask 0x20 during the switch 2 window, which conflicts with switch 1, and saw only mask 0x00 during the switch 9 window. Need a stricter capture/analyzer pass that isolates switch 2 and switch 9, documents whether each physical switch produces a unique switch-mask bit, and updates parser defaults only when evidence is clear.
acceptance_criteria: Switch 2 and switch 9 are each either mapped from repeatable, labeled switch-report evidence or explicitly documented as not exposed/requiring hardware-layout clarification; live bridge issue remains blocked until this is done; parser tests are updated for any newly verified bit mappings.
notes: Strict capture Captures/rk3-switch-2-9.jsonl recorded 102 records across 10 steps. Switch 2 first pass included masks 0x00 and 0x20; switch 2 second pass included mask 0x20. Switch 1 reference emitted no switch report in its own window, but release-all immediately after included mask 0x10. Switch 9 first pass included mask 0x00 only; switch 9 second pass emitted no switch report. Do not proceed to live bridge or parser remap until physical-label ambiguity is resolved.
close_reason: Clean all-switch capture Captures/rk3-all-switches-clean.jsonl recorded 276 records across all 19 release-window steps with no missing windows. Switch 1 emitted mask 0x10; switch 2 emitted mask 0x20 and parser/tests were updated accordingly. Switch 9 toe-down emitted no switch-report mask and only expression movement, so no switch 9 mapping was added; README and Research document this.

title: Perform controlled Rig Kontrol 3 capture
description: Why this issue exists: decoding raw endpoint 0x81 packets requires real hardware actions in known labeled windows; the user is not currently available to operate the switches and pedal. What needs to be done: run the guided capture command while pressing/releasing each labeled switch and sweeping the expression pedal, then run the analyzer and keep/repeat only captures with no missing intended control windows.
acceptance_criteria: Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl exists from a guided run; analyzer output is recorded; each intended switch/toe/expression window has packets; missing expected steps are either resolved by repeating capture or explicitly documented as intentionally unavailable.
notes:
Exact commands: swift run rk3probe --guided-capture --step-seconds 2 --capture-log Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl; then swift run rk3probe --analyze-capture Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl. If the user needs more time per step, use --step-seconds 4. Move only the labeled control in each window.
User ran swift run rk3probe --analyze-capture Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl before the capture file existed; analyzer failed with NSCocoaErrorDomain Code=260 no such file. Next action is to run the guided capture command first.
Initial guided capture exists at Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl and analyzes cleanly for structure: 26 records, all 12 expected steps, no missing windows. It is inconclusive for decoding: baseline-changing offsets are 0 and 6, and every switch/toe/expression step reports candidate offsets: none beyond baseline. Repeat with swift run rk3probe --guided-capture --step-seconds 4 --capture-log Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl and hold each switch through the full labeled window.
Second guided capture at Captures/rk3-guided.jsonl has 343 records, all 12 steps, no missing windows. Evidence: length-8 packets with first byte 0x04 carry switch mask in byte 1; length-33 packets with first byte 0x03 carry expression raw value in bytes 5-6 as a 16-bit big-endian value. Observed switch mask bits in labeled windows: switch 1=0x20, switch 3=0x40, switch 4=0x80, switch 5=0x01, switch 6=0x02, switch 7=0x04, switch 8=0x08. Bit 0x10 was observed during baseline and is likely the missing switch 2 but not verified in its labeled window. Switch 9/toe switch did not produce switch-mask evidence; those need follow-up if the hardware has them. Expression raw observed approx 76...628 during movement.
close_reason: Controlled capture was performed and produced enough evidence to implement the packet parser for switch-mask and expression packets; unresolved physical labels are documented for follow-up rather than blocking parser implementation.

title: Capture and publish physical USB identity through the existing owner
description: Implement one source-faithful physical VID/PID and product/manufacturer/serial capture at the existing successful-parent-open pre-SetConfiguration seam, then publish the coherent USB-generation snapshot read-only via NativeUSB→HAL→NativeClient. This card currently contains a planning-only draft; no code/runtime is executed or automatically authorized. Preserve NI686 request/error/codeunit behavior, existing startup/timing/recovery/ownership and SIP. Native partial/undefined fields are explicit and never fabricated as NI identity.
design:
USB IDENTITY CAPTURE AND PUBLICATION — SMALLEST NEXT IMPLEMENTATION PLAN
2026-10-26. Owning requirement rigkontrol3-40h.2; one planned implementation card under40h, depending on .24 and .25. Planning baseline238f213. This is a Beads-only planning pass: no code, tests/builds, source recovery or live/system actions executed.

PURPOSE AND SOURCE AUTHORITY
Implement exactly one necessary functional operation: capture actual physical USB VID/PID and product/manufacturer/serial metadata on the existing worker, then publish that one-attempt snapshot read-only through NativeUSB→HAL→NativeClient. Retain .24 SPEC14 separately; do not duplicate it, compose the110-byte NI selector3, implement GP/agent construction or claim frontend recognition.
.25 source report ReverseEngineering/NIUSBIdentityAcquisitionContract.md SHA2564a0fc576953cd085c9432a9e49e0b7c36f7fdbbc15f3314073f819be213139fe proves the six methods and exact reader for selected NI-supported OS X10.9.5 / IOUSBFamily686.4.1. NIIdentitySpecificationContract.md SHA256aa5d5ae5aa23b293f4bfe6818b24904c3be5d5aab4a762f9c8e4f83866ce3caf proves S3/serial consumers and ignored string returns. .24's existing metadata cohort/drain/control-lock pattern is implementation authority, not a new lifecycle design. Reuse these reviewed reports and existing source; no fresh binary/metadata recovery or external research is admitted. The older540 reader is not a substitute. No claim about all historical runtimes/subclass overrides or exact NI compiler patch.

WHY THESE PLATFORM CHANGES ONLY
Original physical fields live inside a kernel IOUSBDevice/provider, inaccessible through the accepted SIP-enabled personal-Mac binding. Use its already-retained typed IOUSBDeviceInterface300 on the same owner, implement the proved686 byte reader over synchronous DeviceRequestTO, and add a native cache envelope for the future ARM supporting agent. Do not copy old vtable offsets/object layout into ARM or treat native UID/product labels/registry IDs/constants as physical values. Native generation/availability/error fields communicate this selected cross-process binding safely; they are NOT NI selectors, identity values or new NI policy. Undefined old scratch has no portable faithful byte value; the narrowly defined native availability rule below prevents invented bytes. None of this changes NI ring/calendar/clock/timers/recovery or the original mappings/calibration/LED policy. This is minimum scoped change within the selected binding, not a universal claim about every possible ARM driver.

EXACT CAPTURE POINT, ORDER AND FAILURE POLICY
In existing configure_device(), immediately after successful existing USBDeviceOpen and BEFORE existing SetConfiguration, capture into a worker-local value. No mutex held across getters or synchronous requests. Read actual VID/PID with typed GetDeviceVendor/GetDeviceProduct, then USBGetProductStringIndex+reader, USBGetManufacturerStringIndex+reader, USBGetSerialNumberStringIndex+reader in the original string order. These methods and DeviceRequestTO are the existing pinned IOUSBDeviceInterface300 declarations; no optional alternate API is selected. Index0 is a real value and MUST invoke the same reader. Existing GetConfiguration/advertised checks, SetConfiguration→USBDeviceClose→readback/check→sole-child-discovery/open and EP1/INFO/audio startup order remain unchanged. Parent is CLOSED before child open; no extra open/seize/owner/configuration/reset/vendor/firmware request.
Capture is best-effort metadata, not a new connection success/readiness test. Preserve every typed getter result; accept its output value only on success. If an index getter fails, record that native failure and leave its string unattempted/undefined; do not send a guessed index0, use an old cohort index or add a retry. Continue other fields and existing configuration/startup; no set_error/transport_failed/status/last_error change solely because capture has a failed/undefined field. Do not invent an old cached-getter failure alias. String reader return values remain ignored for connection control, exactly as NI did; retain their raw result and actual defined destination bytes in the native snapshot, including valid empty bytes on error. No requirement that all fields succeed before current generation commit. Device/configuration failures still follow ONLY existing connection/retirement logic.

PROVED READER TO PRESERVE
The small static reader retains the original signed count argument/guard; production capture always passes31 and language0x0409, and count5 is only a source-conformance test. Use valid31-byte destinations and a retained256-byte scratch per string invocation. Preserve source destination-clear timing, type/status/length branches and exact scratch content across requests. Standard IN/device GET_DESCRIPTOR: bmRequestType0x80/bRequest0x06, wValue0x0300|index, wIndex0x0409. Requests are initial2, conditional fallback256, then original initialL; exact-prefix zero before each request, wLenDone reset0, noDataTimeout5000ms/completionTimeout0, synchronous call. At most3 requests/string (9 total); do not claim a finite overall timeout/cancel duration.
Preserve raw e00002c2 guard, initiale00002e8 acceptance ONLY when type3, fallback0/e00002e7, zero initial length early success, type mismatche00002e9, odd originalL retained for final request, final success/type3/even length, signed(even_length-2)<2 empty return, then per-native-little-endian U16 encoding1/2/3 bytes with no surrogate composition/validation/normalization. No reader-side SwapUniWords. Read U16 through memcpy or explicit little-endian byte construction, not unaligned/aliasing casts; this changes representation only. Copy only whole encoded units within count-1. Original loop loads/encodes the NEXT unit BEFORE cumulative-byte budget test; do not stop eagerly at30 bytes. Earlier actual NUL or overflow stops before later units. Preserve zeros/terminator inside bytes0..30 and raw failure returns. Do not access/publish a guessed provider byte31 or invent S3 gap bytes24/45/66/67hex. No NSString/registry-string/singleGET255 replacement, extra language-list query, wLenDone equality rejection, new retry/logging/readiness/abort/timeout rule.
Narrow native definedness rule: initialized scratch prefix=max(all EXACT preceding bzero lengths for this invocation), retaining both bytes and this knowledge across stages. Because each request's entire submitted prefix was just cleared, no wLenDone validation/tracking is needed. Fallback256 permanently makes all256 scratch bytes defined; a later clearL does not discard retained bytes or shrink the known prefix. Before each U16 load the original loop actually reaches, determine whether both bytes are inside this prefix. If it would consume unspecified old scratch, do not read uninitialized C storage or fabricate an old result: stop only local conversion, retain the independently proved raw reader return0 for this post-success path, clear that field's native defined bit and canonicalize its31 transport bytes to0 as INVALID DATA. No new NI error, USB operation, retry, abort, connection failure or early capacity check. Well-defined short/count-mismatch cases continue exactly; partial output in a field marked undefined is not a true empty NI string. Later NI translation of unavailable metadata is separate and unimplemented.

FROZEN NATIVE V1 CONTRACT (ONLY THIS ADDITIVE PROPERTY)
RK3_PROPERTY_USB_IDENTITY=0x6e757362 ('nusb'), GET-only DEVICE/global/main. Keep ninf/nrpt/ncmd/ngai/nspc and all existing sizes/ABI/behavior unchanged. Fixed-width host-endian ARM64 scalars; encoded string bytes are opaque. Add size/offset assertions. No version/package change.
RK3NativeUSBIdentityQuery16: u32 version1@0, u32 reserved0@4, u64 expected_generation(nonzero)@8.
RK3NativeUSBIdentity160: u32 version1@0; int32 native errno status@4; u64 generation@8; u32 attempted_mask@16; u32 defined_mask@20; u16 actualVendorID@24; u16 actualProductID@26; u8 productIndex@28,manufacturerIndex@29,serialIndex@30; reserved byte0@31; int32 raw IOReturn step_status[8]@32..63; product[31]@64; manufacturer[31]@95; serial[31]@126; reserved[3]=0@157..159. Each of these8 raw statuses is the WHOLE operation return (five typed getters and three whole-reader calls), NOT a log of each internal2/256/L USB request. Accepted intermediatee8/e7 can therefore produce a reader result0. Raw IOReturn bit patterns are retained, not translated to errno or NI aliases. No pointers/native object padding.
Bit/step STORAGE order0..7: VendorID,ProductID,productIndex,manufacturerIndex,serialIndex,productReader,manufacturerReader,serialReader. This storage order does NOT reorder execution: productIndex→productReader then manufacturerIndex→manufacturerReader then serialIndex→serialReader. Getter attempted mask0x1f is mandatory; reader pairs are(2,5),(3,6),(4,7). Only low8 bits allowed; defined subset of attempted. Five getters always attempted on a valid selected parent API. Getter defined iff rawstatus0; failed scalar/index output canonical0 INVALID. Reader attempted iff its index getter succeeded (including index0). Its rawstatus is meaningful only when attempted; unattempted reader status0/bytes0 with both bits clear is NOT success. A reader's31 bytes are defined even on its raw nonzero return because the valid destination was cleared; undefined scratch path above is raw0/definedfalse/bytes0. This distinguishes successful empty, ignored legacy failure with defined cleared bytes, unattempted, and unavailable undefined bytes. No Unicode/ASCII filter.
Private int32 rk3_usb_copy_identity(session,expected_generation,RK3NativeUSBIdentity*out): EINVAL for null/gen0; ENODEV if closing/no completed committed capture; then ESTALE if an available cohort differs; failure leaves the whole output unchanged. Status0 copies one canonical160-byte record under existing session mutex. Native availability means completed capture attempt, NOT all fields succeeded. Snapshot remains available with partial/failed fields; no new readiness gate. Native getter/domain errors and raw per-step IOReturn and CoreAudio OSStatus are three distinct domains. No raw IOReturn→NI/errno translation here.
HAL native status values are0/ENODEV/ESTALE only. Status0 requires generation==query.expected_generation!=0 and carries the coherent (possibly partial) captured body. ONLY ENODEV/ESTALE use error envelopes version1/statuserrno with gen0 and ALL body bytes0 (masks, fields,statuses,strings,reserved); these are invalid data, not a physical zero identity. Unsupported private errors are transport failures. Query validation and CFData allocation failures are CoreAudio transport errors with caller payload unchanged. OSStatus0 means only valid transport/envelope, not field success.

COHORT, LOCK AND LIFETIME — REUSE .24, NO NEW FRAMEWORK
Reuse existing spec_collecting and spec_generation as the collecting/committed USB-attempt markers, independent of spec_available. Add only pending/current identity records plus pending-valid and identity-available state; no second generation/epoch, waiter, worker, callback route or timer. At existing spec_begin_attempt_locked clear prior identity validity and start existing collection. After the local synchronous capture finishes, stage only under the existing mutex if that attempt is still collecting and not closing; no late publication after close/revoke. Capture cannot overlap a new attempt on the single worker.
At the existing generation increment/spec_commit_locked critical section, commit completed pending identity to that same nonzero generation, independent of INFO availability. Missing capture remains unavailable without changing connection success. Later INFO can still promote/refresh nspc alone; it neither changes identity nor triggers recapture. Bind identity copy to the same committed spec_generation marker/current generation; no mixed-attempt spec/identity synthesis. Client combining separate nspc/nusb calls must use one expected generation and discard group on any stale/unavailable result; no transactional lifetime promise after return.
Extend the existing spec_revoke_locked metadata action to clear identity pending/current validity at every existing physical-loss, attempt retirement/retry, disconnect and both close paths BEFORE abort/drain/wait/release. Do not revoke on generic diagnostics/audio-only STOP/START/panic/recovery. Old status/info/flags are never provenance. Preserve actual mandatory callback drain before new open; no indistinguishable old callback may cross attempts. Do not rename/refactor unrelated lifecycle or change existing spec behavior.
No session/control mutex while synchronous USB capture waits. Worker/session existing ownership retains parent, local request/scratch/destination buffers and session until calls return; asynchronous cancellation is NOT added. Concurrent close revokes cache immediately but may outlast close_wait's budget while the existing worker reference retains storage. No forced release, close-time shortcut or invented end-to-end deadline. Test an actual held synchronous fake request vs close; after return existing close/configuration/drain flow owns cleanup. Copy readers never own close lifetime; finish calls before releasing the session. No promise of instant unplug detection.
New HAL branch alone: existing control lock pins usb selection→owner session-mutex copy→unlockcontrol BEFORE CFData allocation; no ensure/open, no worker wait/USB/freshness probe inside GET. Absentusb gives canonicalENODEV with no NULL getter. Locked copy is linearization point; whole record or error, no torn fields/use-after-free. Getter/size-discovery/CFData reads add ZERO USB I/O.

EXACT IMPLEMENTATION FILES — FIVE PRODUCTION, TWO EXISTING TESTS, ONE DOC
Driver/NativeControl.h: one selector, two fixed records/bit definitions/assertions only.
Driver/NativeUSB.h: one copy_identity declaration with native/partial/lifetime documentation.
Driver/NativeUSB.c: small static faithful reader/capture helpers on existing typedparent, local initialized-prefix variable, metadata pending/published fields + additions to existing begin/stage/commit/revoke seams and one cache copy. No new module or transport abstraction.
Driver/Audio/RK3AudioDriver.c: sixth custom property metadata (CFPropertyList data AND qualifier), pointer-sized size discovery, GET-only DEVICE/global/main, exact16 query, canonical160 result and existingcontrol→session gate only for this branch.
Driver/NativeClient.h: one typed copy helper using existing rk3_native_copy_blob and temporary160 before output assignment. Validate query, reply version/reserved/status/gen, low8 masks/subset/mandatorygetter attempts/reader eligibility; undefined/unattempted fields canonical0, getter success/defined relation, attempted reader's nonzero status has defined cleared bytes, and defined reader has a NUL inside31. Do not validate UTF8, normalize bytes or require every rawstatus0. Canonical domain errors require entirebody0. Transport/shape failure leaves caller result unchanged; a valid partial/domain-error result is assignable with explicit status/masks.
Driver/Tests/NativeUSBTests.c and Driver/Tests/AudioDriverTests.c: extend existing typed parent mocks and actual owner→productionHAL→NativeClient fixture; no alternate reader/cache model.
ReverseEngineering/NativeUSB.md: document implemented nusb/native availability/cohort/error/undefined-byte limits after implementation.
No NativeHostUSB(.m/.h), NativeAudioISO, DeviceProtocol, MIDI/controller/policy, IPC/GP/agent/frontend, installer, Info.plist, build-script or other production changes. If an admitted file/typedAPI/fixture cannot express the contract, STOP and record exact gap before expanding.

MEANINGFUL RED/GREEN AND ACCEPTANCE — PLANNED, NOT RUN

These are controlled source-derived fixtures, not hardware observations. No fabricated deterministic old uninitialized-byte oracle.

Future fake get*/DeviceRequestTO slots must populate existing small parent tables in every configure fixture; production has no optional-method fallback.
Pending capture is unavailable before existingcommit; captured rawmeta can publish even when same-attempt nspc lacks INFO, and late INFO never recaptures/changes identity. description: Publish the original NI S18 cached14 through the sole native USB owner, a read-only generation-qualified CoreAudio property and typed client; implemented and verified offline only.

SIP and original NI audio/controller behavior remain fixed.

Planned implementation card .24 remains OPEN/UNIMPLEMENTED. New GET-only nspc/device-global-main; query16 and reply32 with version, explicit native errno, coherent generation and opaque14. Preserve old property ABIs. ENODEV/ESTALE native-domain envelopes are distinct from CoreAudio transport failure and NI IOReturn; zero failure payload is invalid data. No new sentinel/mode/topology validation or fake NI identity. Only current parser-accepted INFO bytes enter staged/current cache; valid later INFO refreshes current generation, including legal zero content.

Review closed the state ambiguity: committed generation/marker is separate from availability. Commit without staged INFO does not change existing connection success; later INFO can promote that same cohort to available. Invalidate before retirement/drain/retry/close/known physical transport loss; do not invalidate on generic diagnostics or audio-only state. Existing mandatory drain, not a new callback epoch, prevents old-interface callbacks crossing a new open. Getter uses the existing session mutex; HAL new branch pins usb with existing control→session order and releases before CFData allocation. No worker-only HostInterface/transport_failed access, USB work, timers or instant-unplug promise.

Exact code scope is five production files (NativeControl.h, NativeUSB.h/.c, Audio/RK3AudioDriver.c, NativeClient.h), two existing test files and NativeUSB.md. Tests use the actual NativeClient→production HAL→production owner path and controlled drain/mutex fixtures: exact14, staging/invalidation/promotion/refresh, old/new generation separation, native/transport/shape errors, read-only metadata, malformed safe wrappers, payload-output guards, audio-only retention and zero additional USB/ISO/config/MIDI/LED operations. Synthetic01..0e and allzero vectors are accepted INFO refreshes on an already committed cohort, never startup bypasses. Existing strict arm64 and ASan/UBSan gates plus independent implementation review are required after coding. Preserve HAL written-size convention separately from payload output.

EXACT CARD SCOPE/SCHEMA/TESTS (earlier draft clarifications retained):

PLANNED IMPLEMENTATION ONLY — SPEC14 vertical slice under .2, after .17/.23; no coding/execution in the planning turn.

Purpose: expose the real original S18 14-byte RK3 specification that the selected NativeUSB owner already retains, through one new read-only CoreAudio CFData operation to a typed native client. Complete one necessary owner→HAL→client functional operation; do not implement NI110 identity, physical descriptor/string acquisition, the ARM agent, event registrations, activation/policy changes or a backend/driver migration.

Scope files: Driver/NativeControl.h, NativeUSB.h/.c, Audio/RK3AudioDriver.c, NativeClient.h; existing Driver/Tests/NativeUSBTests.c and AudioDriverTests.c; update NativeUSB.md after implementation. Reuse current test targets. No NativeHostUSB/ISO/ring/calendar/clock/Controller/MIDI behavior, startup USB commands, configuration, retry/timeout, readiness, firmware, signing/install/runtime/security changes.

Frozen native schema: new RK3_PROPERTY_SPEC=0x6e737063 (nspc), DEVICE/global/main, GET-only. Existing ninf/nrpt/ncmd/ngai names/layouts/version unaffected. Query16: U32 version1@0, U32 reserved0@4, U64 expected_generation(nonzero)@8. Reply32: U32 version1@0, I32 native_errno_status@4, U64 generation@8, U8 raw14@16, U8 reserved0[2]@30. Explicit size/offset assertions. Payload bytes are opaque original spec; no zero-sentinel, mode, stereo or content normalization. This is an internal ARM functional record, not an NI IOKit/110-byte ABI emulator.

Three error layers: owner int32 copy_spec(session,expected_gen,out14) uses native errno and only writes out14 on success; bad private args EINVAL; unavailable/closing ENODEV first, otherwise a committed available cohort with wrong generation ESTALE. Success exact14/requested=current committedgeneration. HAL validates exact CFData-wrapped qualifier/type/16byte/version/reserved/nonzero generation and scope/output ABI before owner access. Native domain status0 yields exact raw14/current matchinggen; valid ENODEV/ESTALE produces canonical invalid reply with generation0, raw14/reserved zero, and transport noErr. Those zeros are NOT a valid zero-spec result. Malformed requests/transport/allocation errors return CoreAudio error with caller output untouched. NativeClient validates a temporary32byte CFData reply, version/reserved/recognized status and successgeneration/failurecanonical shape before output assignment; OSStatus reports transport/shape only, Reply.status reports domain. Original NI IOReturn/readiness mapping remains a later adapter step; do not equate these errno/OSStatus namespaces.

Owner lifetime: keep attempt-local staged bytes plus a mutex-protected published cohort; do not treat status.info/info_received/ninf as a coherent lease. Invalidate at new attempt/retry, connection retirement/known physical transport-loss and explicit close BEFORE teardown/drain; no generic set_error/statusFAILED/audio-unpublish invalidation. Commit exact accepted current-attempt INFO14, cohort validity and the existing newly incremented connection generation atomically at existing publication. No extra readiness or USB operation. Later valid INFO in the committed same attempt refreshes the published14 atomically, as original S18 cache does. Callback context is only session: rely on existing mandatory old-I/O drain before a new open, not an invented per-callback epoch. Teardown INFO cannot revalidate; pending old callbacks must block a new commit. Getter never dereferences worker-only HostInterface/transport_failed, never invokes USB/ISO/allocation/sleeps, uses existing session mutex and leaves no borrowed pointer. Cached read linearizes at locked copy; no instantaneous physical-unplug promise. Audio-only stop/start/panic/recovery preserves current USB cohort. NativeAPI caller pins session lifetime.

HAL lifetime: new branch uses existing control mutex around usb pointer selection and bounded owner copy, order control→session mutex; release before CFData allocation/host notification. No ensure_usb/open from a read, no claim that old getters already use this gate, no broad HAL lifecycle repair. Advertise both property and qualifier CFPropertyList types, pointer-size property value, reject setters. Existing consumers and all old properties unchanged.

RED/GREEN proof at actual seams: extend existing NativeClient→production HAL→production NativeUSB integration, not a serializer-only mirror. REVIEW CLARIFICATIONS BEFORE CODE: tests use only NULL/wrong-sized qualifier wrappers or valid CF objects of wrong type, never arbitrary invalid-address dereferences. No tests claim old callbacks can arrive after completed mandatory drain. Allzero content-success case is a valid same-cohort INFO refresh, not a fabricated successful startup.

FINAL STATE/ERROR REVIEW CLARIFICATION BEFORE CODE: distinguish committed-cohort identity from published availability. Existing successful generation publication must always record that still-current attempt's committed generation/marker, even if no metadata stage exists; then spec availability remains false without failing the existing connection. A later accepted INFO in that committed collecting attempt must atomically promote unavailable→available at the SAME generation, or refresh existing bytes. Revocation clears collection, pending validity, committed marker and availability; it never permits teardown INFO to promote. This uses an existing-generation marker, not a new per-callback epoch/counter. Add the exact missing-stage commit→later valid INFO→same-generation success regression.
Private NULL session, NULL out14 or generation0 returns EINVAL without payload writes. HAL absent globalusb returns the canonical ENODEV domain envelope without calling the private getter on NULL. Only0/ENODEV/ESTALE enter a normal Reply; any unexpected private status is a CoreAudio/internal transport failure, not a new domain/NI code. Preserve canonical error generation0/zero-invalid payload and distinct OSStatus, native errno and NI IOReturn namespaces.

Scope and boundary
This is a bounded read-only check of official Apple documentation and Apple Staff guidance current at this assessment. No developer-account access, certificate request, private-key export/use, signing, download/install, build, kext load, USB/audio/MIDI client, service or security change was performed. 1. Native architecture is separate from signing
Apple requires Apple Silicon kexts to contain arm64e, including pointer authentication and kernel restrictions. The current user-space arm64 HAL/MIDI artifacts are therefore not evidence that a reconstructed kernel executable is ABI-correct, linked, or loadable. This requirement does not prove that the entire original audio implementation must become a user HAL. Source: Apple, Implementing drivers, system extensions, and kexts, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/implementing-drivers-system-extensions-and-kexts .

2. Normal signed deployment: special certificate, not an ordinary app identity
Apple's current notarization documentation explicitly permits kext distribution using a Developer ID Application certificate with the kext capability. The corresponding Apple-issued leaf certificate has both Developer ID Application OID 1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13 and kext OID 1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.18. Ordinary Developer ID Application has .13 without the required kext extension; Developer ID Installer (.14) is for packages, not the kext executable. The published Developer ID CPS v3.2 (June 2, 2021), section 4.11.3, specifies both .13/.18 as mandatory critical certificate extensions plus code-signing EKU 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3. This older published profile is corroborated by current Apple Staff guidance below; no claim is made that v3.2 is the latest CPS. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/resolving-common-notarization-issues ; https://images.apple.com/certificateauthority/pdf/Apple_Developer_ID_CPS_v3.2.pdf .

The kext authorization is in an Apple-issued certificate. A locally added entitlements plist or provisioning profile cannot manufacture that CA-issued extension. Apple Development uses a distinct WWDR trust path; its acceptance by MIDIServer for this project's plug-in does not establish kext capability. TN3127 identifies ordinary Developer ID's issuer OID .100.6.2.6 and Apple Development's WWDR issuer .100.6.2.1. OID inspection is meaningful only with the Apple certificate chain; an arbitrary issuer could copy the same OID. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements .

3. Current Apple Staff confirmation, with eligibility limits
In July 2026, Apple DTS confirmed that an ordinary Developer ID Application certificate remains insufficient for kext notarization. DTS says kext signing approval historically went to corporate, not individual/personal, accounts and that new requests are unlikely to be approved. That is current first-party guidance about the approval path, not a determination of this user's account type, existing permissions, or the outcome of a future application. No account was inspected and no approval request is authorized. A previously issued ordinary certificate does not become kext-enabled merely because a later account approval exists: the signing leaf must actually include .18. Sources: Apple Staff replies in https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391 and the linked Apple DTS certificate-inspection guidance https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/52353 .

4. Signed deployment versus temporary personal testing
For normally distributable kexts, DTS specifies a kext-enabled Developer ID signature plus notarization and the required reduced startup security. Apple's installation documentation separately requires Apple Silicon user consent, third-party-kext allowance, auxiliary kext-collection rebuild and reboot. Reduced Security is not a substitute for a missing kext-capable certificate or notarization. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391 ; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/installing-a-custom-kernel-extension .

The same July 2026 DTS reply explicitly distinguishes personal development: its stated current Apple Silicon path is SIP disabled plus Permissive Security in recoveryOS, rather than notarizing a personal product with an ordinary app certificate. Apple's September 17, 2026 deployment guide describes Reduced and Permissive as different policies and says SIP must be off before enabling Permissive. This is a materially different testing condition, not an approved normal-deployment result or evidence that this user accepts it. No policy-modification commands are proposed or executed here. ## Availability and admission are separate

The completed static audit found real arm64e IOAudioFamily code in this Mac's
boot collection and defined matches for 184 of 186 original audio-family
imports. Retaining IOAudioDevice/IOAudioEngine while replacing legacy USB with
kernel IOUSBHostFamily remains the smallest structural candidate identified;
that is not a loading, signing or stability guarantee. Exact hashes and
comparison limits remain in the parity audit and `.13`.

Apple classifies legacy **IOUSBFamily as unsupported since macOS 11**, whereas
**IOAudioFamily is deprecated since 12.3**. Its published policy says deprecated
KPI kexts do not load by default; its footnote exempts SIP-disabled or
MDM-approved kexts from deprecation-policy enforcement. Thus the deprecated
category is neither an ARM availability proof nor an unrestricted admission
promise. Applying that published default to this new IOAudioFamily driver is
a policy inference, not an observed macOS 27.0.1 load attempt.
[Apple deprecated-kext policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

The same page's USB vendor-specific IPC restriction is conditional on the
driver not tying into an IOFamily subsystem. The original audio driver does
tie into IOAudioFamily. That prevents automatically treating it as a standalone
USB IPC case, but does not establish approval for a newly reconstructed driver.
[Apple USB policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

Apple requires arm64e for Apple Silicon kexts and limits kernel extensions
where an equivalent system-extension solution exists. These are constraints
on the candidate, not proof that this particular NI implementation has an

## Security modes and policy exceptions

For ordinary signed third-party kext installation, Apple documents enabling
kexts through recoveryOS, Reduced Security, authorization and an AuxKC rebuild
and restart. With SIP enabled, signatures are checked before inclusion; with
SIP disabled, that signature check is not enforced. An authorized list can
still contain kexts excluded from the resulting collection.
[Apple kernel-extension security](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/security/sec8e454101b/web)

**Reduced Security and SIP disabled are different conditions.** Apple's
current startup-policy guide distinguishes Full, Reduced and Permissive
Security. The personal-development route must not be described as
ordinary Reduced Security. An MDM exception to deprecation policy likewise
does not manufacture a valid signing identity, working native code or user
consent. No MDM enrollment/profile is being proposed or applied here.
[Apple startup security, published 2026-09-17](https://support.apple.com/en-ca/guide/deployment/dep5810e849c/web)

## Signing: distributable and personal paths

Apple's signing guidance identifies a kext-enabled Developer ID Application
certificate by its kext extension OID **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.18**, in addition
to the Developer ID Application extension **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13**.
Ordinary app signing is not equivalent. This older DTS reference is corroborated by the July 2026

[Apple DTS signing reference](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/52353),
[Apple Developer ID certificate profile, v3.2 §4.11.3](https://images.apple.com/certificateauthority/pdf/Apple_Developer_ID_CPS_v3.2.pdf).
The profile is a published historical certificate specification, corroborated
by the current staff guidance; it is not presented as the latest CPS.

Apple's notarization documentation requires new or updated kexts to be
notarized for its distributable path and specifies the appropriate Developer

identity or for startup/loading approval.

## Availability and admission are separate

The completed static audit found real arm64e IOAudioFamily code in this Mac's
boot collection and defined matches for 184 of 186 original audio-family
imports. Retaining IOAudioDevice/IOAudioEngine while replacing legacy USB with
kernel IOUSBHostFamily remains the smallest structural candidate identified;
that is not a loading, signing or stability guarantee. Exact hashes and
comparison limits remain in the parity audit and `.13`.

Apple classifies legacy **IOUSBFamily as unsupported since macOS 11**, whereas
**IOAudioFamily is deprecated since 12.3**. Its published policy says deprecated
KPI kexts do not load by default; its footnote exempts SIP-disabled or
MDM-approved kexts from deprecation-policy enforcement. Thus the deprecated
category is neither an ARM availability proof nor an unrestricted admission
promise. Applying that published default to this new IOAudioFamily driver is
a policy inference, not an observed macOS 27.0.1 load attempt.
[Apple deprecated-kext policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

The same page's USB vendor-specific IPC restriction is conditional on the
driver not tying into an IOFamily subsystem. The original audio driver does
tie into IOAudioFamily. That prevents automatically treating it as a standalone
USB IPC case, but does not establish approval for a newly reconstructed driver.
[Apple USB policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

## Four independent gates

| Gate | What the primary evidence establishes | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native API/ABI | Original kernel code needs arm64e/PAC and a replacement for legacy USB. | That an x86 binary, old vtable layout or decompiler casts can be transplanted. |
| Deprecated-KPI policy | Default enforcement and the published SIP/MDM exceptions are separate from API presence. | That ordinary manual approval or Reduced Security alone overrides deprecation policy. |
| Signing and distribution | A suitable kext-enabled signing identity and the relevant distribution checks are distinct requirements. | That an Apple Development or ordinary Developer ID identity is sufficient. |
| Startup/user authorization | Apple Silicon kext installation uses explicit authorization, an auxiliary collection and a restart. | Consent to alter this Mac's security or proof that its present startup policy permits the candidate. |

Apple requires arm64e for Apple Silicon kexts and limits kernel extensions
where an equivalent system-extension solution exists. These are constraints
on the candidate, not proof that this particular NI implementation has an
approved equivalent or that a particular replacement is the minimum change.
[Apple implementation guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/implementing-drivers-system-extensions-and-kexts)

## Security modes and policy exceptions

For ordinary signed third-party kext installation, Apple documents enabling
kexts through recoveryOS, Reduced Security, authorization and an AuxKC rebuild
and restart. With SIP enabled, signatures are checked before inclusion; with
SIP disabled, that signature check is not enforced. An authorized list can
still contain kexts excluded from the resulting collection.
[Apple kernel-extension security](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/security/sec8e454101b/web)

**Reduced Security and SIP disabled are different conditions.** Apple's
current startup-policy guide distinguishes Full, Reduced and Permissive
Security. The personal-development route must not be described as
ordinary Reduced Security. An MDM exception to deprecation policy likewise
does not manufacture a valid signing identity, working native code or user
consent. No MDM enrollment/profile is being proposed or applied here.
[Apple startup security, published 2026-09-17](https://support.apple.com/en-ca/guide/deployment/dep5810e849c/web)

## Signing: distributable and personal paths

Apple's signing guidance identifies a kext-enabled Developer ID Application
certificate by its kext extension OID **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.18**, in addition
to the Developer ID Application extension **1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13**.
Ordinary app signing is not equivalent. This older DTS reference is corroborated by the July 2026
staff answer below; no account request or certificate operation occurred.
[Apple DTS signing reference](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/52353),
[Apple Developer ID certificate profile, v3.2 §4.11.3](https://images.apple.com/certificateauthority/pdf/Apple_Developer_ID_CPS_v3.2.pdf).
The profile is a published historical certificate specification, corroborated
by the current staff guidance; it is not presented as the latest CPS.

Apple's notarization documentation requires new or updated kexts to be
notarized for its distributable path and specifies the appropriate Developer
ID certificate types. Notarization is not a replacement for the right signing
identity or for startup/loading approval.
[Apple notarization requirements](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution),
[Apple kext certificate diagnostics](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/resolving-common-notarization-issues)

In **July 2026**, Apple DTS CoreOS/Hardware engineer Kevin Elliott addressed
personal-use Apple Silicon kexts directly: the testing path requires SIP
disabled and Permissive Security. He reported that kext-signing approval had
been limited to corporate accounts and new requests were unlikely. Quinn
separately distinguished distributable signing/notarization from personal
testing. These are current, attributable staff statements, not a guarantee
about this user's account or future decisions. Only the Apple staff replies,
not the questioner's reported experiment, support this conclusion.
[Apple DTS personal-use clarification](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/837391)

Instructions590d..5920 initialize ALL64 four-byte gain slots at+bc58 to0x3f800000 (Float32 unity), not only active channels. Otherwise BadArgument e00002c2 and leaves storage unchanged. Wrapper9850 checks device+engine; absence returns NotAttached e00002d9. Scalar slots are64bits wide: channel is lowU32 of scalar0 and value bits lowU32 of scalar1 at+8; do not cast that scalar to a numeric float value.
- Getter8930: accept iff channel<64 AND channel<inputCount; copy four stored bytes unchanged, otherwise BadArgument. Wrapper9890 requires device+engine and returns NotAttached if absent. Setter and getter bounds are deliberately recorded separately; do not normalize both to inputCount because that would change the original shared-family API.
- Bounds examples: attached RK3(2in,2out) accepts set/get0,1 and rejects2/63/64/UINT32_MAX. (0,0) rejects all. (0,2) permits set0,1 but no getter. (1,1) pairCount0 means no set, while get0 can read default unity. (3,0) permits set0,1 and get0,1,2; slot2 stays default unless another legitimate original update occurs. (1,4) permits set0..3 but get0 only. Inputs/outputs64 or larger still cap every public index at63. Negative signed input encoded asU32 wraps and is rejected by this unsigned check. Do not claim current native driver supports these other topologies; its device admission remains verified stereo. Wider examples are original predicate tests.
- Numeric input domain is all2^32 Float32 BIT PATTERNS. No numeric clamp, finite check, sign restriction or dB conversion is in these methods. +0/-0, finite negative/amplifying/subnormal values, +/-Inf and quiet/signaling NaN payloads all survive SET->GET bit-for-bit. Property encoding must carry aU32 value_bits and use memcpy/integers; converting through double, decimal text or floating comparison would risk changing a NaN/-0 bit pattern.
- convertInputSamples6e90/6f18 calls AppleConvertInputSamplesc550, then applyGainc650 at6f41 and returns the converter status. The host destination is a contiguous Float32 stereo buffer; firstSampleFrame locates packed capture, but c650 does not add that offset again. For each stereo frame multiply left by its Float32 gain and right by its Float32 gain (MULSS), with no limiter/clamp/ramp/dB conversion. c650 returns without touching destination when BOTH gain values are ordered-equal1.0; this preserves raw destination bits including unusual sample values for the unity fast path. Otherwise even the channel whose gain is1 passes through multiplication when the other channel differs. Gains are reloaded during the original loop; native coherent per-callback snapshot is a stated concurrency binding, not an instruction-by-instruction timing claim.
- IEEE multiplication can produce infinities/NaNs and signed zeros. Preserve arithmetic intent/class/sign and exact gain storage. Do not promise x86SSE versus ARM bit-identical NaN payload propagation, signaling exception flags or subnormal handling without actual FP-environment evidence. description: The user asks whether the primary lift-and-shift is complete and requires planning and Beads capture before any further path. The answer is no: the current native implementation passes substantial functional checks, but original-capability and timing/platform parity are incomplete. Produce the complete original-to-ARM inventory and necessary-binding decision before any further implementation or runtime experiment.
design:
GOVERNING PLAN — ORIGINAL NI RK3 LIFT-AND-SHIFT
User clarification, 2026-10-25: the primary objective is a lift-and-shift, not a replacement design. Before any new path, finish the necessary planning and capture it in Beads. This plan is the next gate. It does not authorize speculative tuning, a new backend, a new UI or further ad-hoc hardware experiments.

Definition of complete
Preserve the original RK3 driver behavior and externally needed capabilities on the attached Apple Silicon Mac. Recover behavior from the exact original binaries and instruction evidence, then change only what ARM and the current macOS interfaces demonstrably require. Original ring, packing, sample positions, clocks, queue calendar, error policies and recovery are the reference. Every necessary platform substitution must have a written reason and a test. A working prototype, decompiled functions, successful compilation or a few functional tests do not alone mean this objective is complete.

Current evidence boundary
The original audio 2.8.0 and MIDI 2.8.0 binaries were decompiled and cross-checked. Native ARM audio/MIDI components are built and installed. Version 0.2.0 passed subjective clear guitar at unity gain/128 frames, eight switches, expression range, local LEDs, incoming LED feedback and held-switch USB recovery. Version 0.2.1/build6 is now installed with all 12 files and signatures verified against manifest e2ee623f97af89c24d94e38d7061b460c3e1bd51dd13052d57b9937ecaa400e6. Its 120-second silent run passed, but its longer MIDI-active run failed after 227.593 seconds with TooOld. Thus stability and full timing parity remain incomplete. The ordering defect (.12) and audio-only recovery mapping (.8) are completed components; their closure does not close the primary objective.

Stage 1 — bounded parity inventory; the only next work
Use the existing original binaries, manifests, decompilation exports, assembly, SDK evidence and current source. Do not modify/install drivers, change scheduling, change queue lead, or start a new runtime experiment during this inventory.
Classify each sub-behavior and failure branch separately; matching command bytes must not conceal different readiness/failure policy. For each row record: original capability/method and image-relative address; evidence confidence; corresponding ARM code; status (matched, implemented/unverified, missing, or necessary substitution/unresolved); exact difference; current test/physical evidence; linked Beads issue; and completion/stop criteria.
Cover:
A. USB discovery/configuration, endpoint ownership, device information, initialization commands and conditional firmware-update behavior for this RK3.
B. Audio formats/rates/channels, conversion/check bytes, host-addressed rings, priming, descriptor ownership, IN/OUT calendars, latency/sample offset, timestamps, input polling and inactive-output clearing.
C. Kernel workloop/scheduling assumptions, panic delays, stop/drain, device removal, sleep/wake and original error classifications.
D. CoreMIDI DIN ABI, parser/packetization, port identity, send failures, client activation and delivery lifetime.
E. Raw controller reports, original mapper provenance, eight switches, expression calibration, toe/external inputs, assignments and incoming LED behavior.
F. Host/client-facing contracts. Distinguish ordinary CoreAudio/CoreMIDI compatibility from the original NI private user-client/control interfaces. Record what is required for the user's Guitar Rig/VST use and what is not yet demonstrated. Do not assume generic MIDI access proves every original NI-client interaction; do not start an NI compatibility layer or editor project merely because a private interface exists.
G. Installation, signing, rollback and limitations.
This is an audit of the attached RK3's original capability surface, not a port of unrelated NI device families or a new feature wish list.

Stage 2 — justify the architecture/platform substitutions
Before more timing work, account for the existing kernel IOAudioEngine/IOUSBPipe -> AudioServerPlugIn/IOUSBHost user-process substitution. Establish from current ARM/macOS availability and original dependencies which changes are unavoidable and which are our choices. Resolve the lowest-change supported binding using a bounded, read-only feasibility check; do not open a new implementation branch/backend/security change as part of the check. Record any signing, entitlement or security requirement before considering that route. The feasibility check is one bounded read-only evidence pass over pinned original dependencies, current local ARM/macOS artifacts/SDK and directly relevant official platform documentation. It must not install/download a new toolchain, request entitlements, load a driver, change security or start implementation. Stop when these sources cannot answer a required question; record the exact missing evidence/access and a narrow follow-up card rather than extending the search. Header presence/absence alone is not a complete feasibility proof. The output must be a written Architecture Necessity Decision in Beads before selecting another runtime measurement or implementation path; incompatibility with our chosen user process is not proof that choosing that process was unavoidable.
Known unresolved assumptions include modern primary-interrupt publication timing, last-output-client activity equivalence, sleep/wake behavior and the scheduling-domain change from the original kernel workloop. Shared KernelUserShared allocation does not prove exact primary cadence. A 54.5 ms handoff interval does not alone prove that changing QoS is the answer.

Stage 3 — implement only identified original parity gaps
Create or refine a child issue for each missing original behavior. For example, the ARM driver currently exposes only stereo 48 kHz, while NI advertised 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96 and 192 kHz; restoring those is original parity, not a new audio feature. Preserve all applicable original protocol values and transformations.
Complete confirmed missing original behavior with the minimum justified ARM/macOS adapter. Do not substitute a new queue algorithm, guessed delay, UI, generic bridge or speculative recovery policy. If an original capability is deliberately excluded, the primary objective cannot be called full parity without the user's explicit acceptance of that narrower scope.

Stage 4 — validate/fix necessary bindings using one bounded path at a time
The late-request fault (.11) is a timing-parity blocker, not an invitation to general performance optimization. Before its next action, write a branch card containing:
1. The exact original behavior/parity row being preserved.
2. The observed failure and evidence, with facts separated from inference.
3. One falsifiable hypothesis and the reason it is the next highest-value one.
4. One minimal measurement or correction and its scope/cost.
5. The red/green command, exact duration/repetition count, error predicate, success threshold and stop/escalation condition;120 seconds already passed before a227.593-second failure, so the word sustained alone is insufficient.
6. Why this is necessary for ARM/current macOS rather than a new design.
Current measured fault: NI requeue target remains exactly old frame+64; observed completion-to-enqueue entry was about 65.94 ms, with a 54.54 ms raw-handler-to-worker interval and 17.70 ms elapsed enqueue call. Ordered hold was negligible and no FIFO backlog was present. This localizes the miss but does not distinguish worker CPU work, blocking, descheduling or publication delay.
Candidate next measurements are not approved decisions yet: a narrowly scoped stack/scheduler capture, or bounded self-CPU/phase observations if access is unavailable. Select ONE only after Stages 1–2 and record its gate. Do not run parallel speculative sampling/QoS/backend branches. No numeric priority, private interrupt flag or queue-lead tuning without evidence. Stop a branch if it cannot distinguish the hypothesis, changes unrelated behavior, or requires a broader architecture/security decision; record that result instead of extending the rabbit hole.

Stage 5 — original-capability acceptance and cleanup
Automated tests must compare original-derived vectors, actual callback ownership/order, clocks and failure policies at the real seam. Installed acceptance must cover sustained clear audio with all eight switches, expression and LED feedback; every restored original format/rate; reconnect, Stop/Start, sleep/wake and inactive-output behavior. DIN/toe/external inputs need the appropriate physical setup; record unavailable hardware as unvalidated rather than inventing success.
Remove temporary DEBUG timing instrumentation after causal verification. Run final signed package, rollback, strict and sanitizer gates, then installed acceptance on the clean build. Commit/push code and export/sync Beads. Close the parent only when the matrix is satisfied or the user has explicitly accepted documented exceptions.

Branch admission rule
Every subsequent path must already have its original-parity justification, bounded plan, evidence, test, stop criterion and Beads link before execution. This task produces the matrix and necessary-binding decision; it is not complete merely because this plan has been written.
acceptance_criteria: A complete attached-RK3 original-to-ARM parity matrix exists in Beads, with instruction/source references and current status/evidence for every capability group. Original missing functionality and unresolved platform substitutions are explicitly distinguished from completed implementation. The existing kernel-to-user architecture choice has a bounded evidence-based necessity assessment. Each remaining child issue has a minimum plan, red/green evidence and a stop criterion before work resumes. No new driver implementation, sampling/QoS experiment or backend/security change occurs during this audit. The parent remains incomplete until parity is demonstrated or the user explicitly accepts exceptions.

1. Necessary: replace the x86_64 execution/ABI with native implementation. An Apple-Silicon kernel extension must target arm64e/PAC, whereas a user-process ARM plug-in targets its documented user ABI; simply relabeling or recompiling an unchanged decompiler/vtable-offset dump is not a port.

Apple documents all IOUSBFamily KPIs unsupported since macOS11, the current ARM boot collection has no com.apple.iokit.IOUSBFamily entry, and selectedSDK27.0 lacks legacy IOUSBDevice/IOUSBPipe/IOUSBInterface kernel headers. The new kernel IOUSBHostFamily APIs and user IOUSBHost APIs are distinct possible bindings, not interchangeable proof of necessity for either entire architecture.
3. NOT established necessary: replace IOAudioDevice/IOAudioEngine with AudioServerPlugIn. The actual current arm64e boot collection contains real IOAudioFamily code and exact definitions for184/186 original audio-family imports. Current SDK declares original audio classes, with deprecation warnings. Therefore the existing user-HAL is an architecture choice whose minimum-change necessity is unproved, not an ARM requirement already established by this audit.
4. Minimum structural-change candidate supported by the inspected public interfaces: retain reconstructed IOAudioDevice/IOAudioEngine/sample-positioned ring/workloop/lifecycle behavior and replace only the legacyUSB binding with kernel IOUSBHostFamily, plus arm64e source/ABI updates. This is a CONDITIONAL CANDIDATE, NOT a claim a new third-party kext is policy-approved, buildable, loadable or stable. It avoids making scheduling domain, privateIPC replacement, host-buffer metadata and output-client activity mappings into assumptions merely because userHAL was chosen. It must pass the access/signing/policy gate below before any implementation decision. No reflex DriverKit choice is made; Apple's recommendation alone is not proof it preserves these NI contracts with fewer changes.

## Architecture Necessity Decision

The original plist depends on **IOAudioFamily**, **IOUSBFamily** and kernel

IOAudioFamily is deprecated rather than identically classified as unsupported.
New deprecated-kext loading is constrained by current policy. Neither a missing
header nor deprecation alone proves that an audio class is absent from ARM.
[Apple kernel-extension policy](https://developer.apple.com/support/kernel-extensions)

The actual Mac is **macOS 27.0.1 / 26A434 / arm64**, with **Xcode 27.1 /
27A9275** and selected **macOS SDK 27.0**. The audit inspected the real boot
collection, rather than assuming a bundle directory contained executable code:

**Required changes:** native execution/source ABI, including ARM replacements
for x86-specific code; and migration away from the unsupported legacy USB
family. Apple requires the kernel's arm64e/PAC ABI for Apple Silicon kexts;
user-process plug-ins use their documented native ABI.
[Apple driver implementation guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions/implementing-drivers-system-extensions-and-kexts)

**Minimum structural-change candidate:** retain reconstructed
`IOAudioDevice`/`IOAudioEngine`, its sample-positioned ring, workloop and
lifecycle, replacing the USB binding with **kernel IOUSBHostFamily** and the
required source/ABI changes. This is an engineering inference from the inspected
contracts, not a validated or policy-approved deployment recommendation.
The SDK's kernel `IOUSBHostPipe` documents legacy-pipe migration, ISO I/O using
caller-owned lists/storage, and `clearStall(bool withRequest)`; that Boolean
choice is closer to NI's calls than the current user API.

**Not justified as unavoidable:** replacing the kernel audio model with the
current AudioServerPlugIn, default pthread/dispatch handoff, new inter-bundle
CFData transport and approximated host activity/power events. Those changes
may require a deployment rationale, but “ARM has no IOAudioEngine” is false on
this inspected Mac. A user-API limitation does not prove that selecting that
API was necessary.

**Unresolved deployment gate:** a new driver using deprecated IOAudioFamily
must satisfy current loading policy, suitable signing authorization and the
user's security constraints. General Apple Silicon kext installation involves
approval, auxiliary collection rebuilding/restart and Reduced Security settings;
Reduced Security alone does not prove this specific deprecated-family driver
will be admitted. The audit did not inspect/change startup security, request
signing authorization, install a KDK or compile/load a kext. The absence of a
local KDK is a tooling observation, not an impossibility proof.
[Apple custom-kext installation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/installing-a-custom-kernel-extension),
[Apple deployment requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/deployment/depa5fb8376f/web)

**Disposition:** the bounded necessity assessment stops here. Beads **`.17`**
requires one explicit minimum-change deployment/binding decision before coding
or timing work. It must use the actual constraints above. It cannot silently
continue the current HAL, start another backend, reduce security or select
DriverKit merely because the original family is deprecated.

title: Preserve NI completion order across the modern USB callback binding
description: A production-ISO fake-host reproduction with whole-IRP primary publication and only1ms delay on slot0 exposes an introduced ready-FIFO/consumed-epoch dependency cycle when tied callbacks arrive slot1 before slot0. At bus5198 FIFO=[1,0], read_cursor0 alreadyconsumed; slot0 requeue needed to advance cursor sits behind blocked slot1. After128ms all64 inputs stall with no panic. Same delay with calendar-order delivery runs20s. Original NI readHandler directly scans then requeues; it has no new epoch/FIFO wait. Restore the original implicit per-pipe ordered completion contract in the current USB binding, preserving NI ring/calendar and buffer lifetime. This deterministic deadlock is not yet linked to the separate live TooOld fault (.11).
acceptance_criteria: Actual Host adapter tests first go RED for out-of-order system completion delivery. Per-pipe successful ISO callback delivery follows submission acceptance order with exactly-once callbacks, including abort/failure/zero requests and reentrant enqueue. The production-ISO advancing-bus counterexample is GREEN under the promised ordered binding. Strict/ASan/UBSan and independent review pass; no calendar lead or sample-placement changes. This confirms that our previous adapter did not provide the order needed by the NI-derived cyclic input ring. The public serial-queue contract serializes execution but does not establish chronological per-request completion delivery.

Scope and attribution boundary
This is a hardware-free reproduction of a newly identified permanent audio-input completion dependency cycle. It is not evidence that this cycle caused the separate installed0.2.0 XHCI kIOReturnIsoTooOld errors recorded in .11. The deterministic cycle produces diagnostic0, no panic, and a stalled engine; the live failure produced TooOld and an audio-only restart. Keep those signatures and their causality separate.

Exact event model
Bus begins1000; preserve NI startup/calendar: initial IN1101..1164; first requeued IN/OUT1165 onward. Whole eight-transaction primary status/count publication occurs independently at request.start_frame+1ms. Only slot0's raw completion callback has1ms additional delay; all other input callbacks have0ms additional delay. Output callbacks retire at output.start_frame+1ms; worker service runs every simulated millisecond, with additional CaptureAt128-frame polling every3ms. Every delivery checks the transfer still has the event's saved scheduled frame, preventing a reentrant new submission from receiving an obsolete event. No worker starvation or altered queue lead is injected. Raw tied completions are delivered reverse slot order in RED, so slot1 retires before slot0. GREEN changes only that tied-delivery ordering to forward slot order, so slot0 retires first. API acceptance-order delivery is the proposed modern binding contract; no NI calendar or sample-placement change is needed for that contract.

Minimal deterministic cycle
At bus5198 (4.198 simulated seconds after bus1000), next global IN target5260 is still62ms ahead. Total IN submissions4159.
FIFO index0: slot1, saved received frame5197, callback due5198, added lag0ms, input_epoch65, consumed_epoch64.
FIFO index1: slot0, saved received frame5196, callback due5198, added lag1ms, input_epoch64, consumed_epoch64.
Read cursor is slot0/microframe0. consume_input_locked returns because consumed_epoch[0]==input_epoch[0]. FIFO head1 cannot be requeued until its epoch65 has been decoded. Cursor0 cannot advance to slot1 until slot0 is requeued; the callback permitting that requeue sits at FIFO index1 behind head1. This is a closed dependency cycle.
After128 additional simulated milliseconds: ready_count64; zero pending input requests; submissions still4159; stream_error0; panicfalse. All outstanding input callbacks have retired, so no future input completion can unblock the head. Stop/drain/destruction still pass.
GREEN control runs20,000 simulated milliseconds with19,962 IN submissions, max_ready0 and max_head_wait0. Independent random-order searches (200 seeds each for input callback jitter0..8,0..16,0..32,0..63ms) reached dependency stalls before TooOld; they do not establish a past-frame enqueue or link to live .11.

Current source conditions
Driver/NativeAudioISO.c at checkpoint:
- line176: input scanner returns at an already-consumed epoch (or incomplete whole primary batch).
- lines279–280: ready FIFO head waits until that slot's current epoch has been consumed.
- lines325–327: read_complete appends in callback-arrival order and services that FIFO.
- lines306–310: list reset/epoch increment/requeue happen only after the gate passes.
Each guard has a local purpose, but callback-order inversions allow their dependency cycle. This is not a ring capacity or extra calendar-lead problem.

Independent Host reviewer inspected local public IOUSBHost headers. The examined isochronous enqueue/list/completion documentation contains no per-pipe chronological callback-delivery guarantee. The adapter must uphold its explicit successful-submission acceptance-order callback contract if the ISO layer depends on it; actual Host adapter tests are assigned to a different agent and are required before claiming this issue fixed.

title: Account for original NI command recovery and current API differences
description: Original EP1 error classifications/no-replay behavior are implemented and tested. Current public clear-stall resets both endpoint and controller and aborts pending I/O, whereas original NI recovery sometimes cleared only controller state; retirement gating handles the chosen API safely. This remains an explicit difference to justify under .13, not a claim of exact original semantics. Startup failure gates and unconditional merged controller activation also need branch-level parity accounting. Physical functionality passed; no further experimental path until the canonical audit gate.
notes:
Original MIDI Send0x2720 returns selector4 error without publishing device offline. Audio user-client MIDIWrite0x9450 calls void deviceMIDIWrite0x2990 and returns success while the provider exists, discarding sendCommand failure. The current native output_worker record_io_failure latches failed_generation indefinitely after one command error; that is a fidelity defect once EP1 recovery preserves the generation. Narrow fix: no replay, drop failed output entry, allow later entries and controller input; actual offline follows provider removal/discovery. Keep malformed input/IPC validation separate.
READ-ONLY ORIGINAL POWER/EP1 FINDINGS — 2026-10-25

Severity correction: the earlier review observation that command_suspended can remain set after NotResponding is a real current state-machine property, but it is NOT established as a divergence from NI. No explicit original wake-driven EP1 read rearm was found. Do not invent a blanket power-notification retry or describe one as recovered NI behavior.

Original NIUSBAudioDevice::performPowerStateChange at0x1fe0 calls the base IOAudioDevice implementation first. On transition from state0 to state1 or2, instructions0x2023..0x2039 invoke provider-device virtual slot+0x988 with false, then+0x950 with a two-byte local status pointer. Anchoring the known GetVendorID/GetProductID slots0x8f0/0x8f8 against Apple's published IOUSBDevice virtual declaration order resolves these to SuspendDevice(false), then GetDeviceStatus(USBStatus*). The override then calls initialized engine awakeFromSleep0xbcb0. A transition to state0 calls engine enterSleep0xbc50. The provider calls are not command-IN read submissions.

Original enterSleep0xbc50 cancels the timestamp timer at engine+0xbd98 and zeros USB/host anchor and prior-measurement fields+0xbd70/+0xbd78/+0xbd80/+0xbd88. Original awakeFromSleep0xbcb0 resets refresh counter+0xbd90 and scaled interval+0xbd58 to10000000000, calls clearSampleBufferForStream0x7510 for the output groups, updates USB-cycle timing, establishes a fresh anchor and rearms timestamp maintenance at128ms while the device remains initialized/present. It has no direct EP1 read/rearm call.

A search across all241 private original C-like exports for the command-IN pipe member+0x920 and its Read virtual slot+0x1d0 found submissions in initHardware0x0db0 and the ordinary commandReplyDispatch0x20e0 tail. No additional direct NI wake submission was found. commandReplyDispatch's NotResponding branch aborts command IN and OUT and returns without entering the rearm tail; Aborted also returns. Current NativeUSB deliberately mirrors that no-rearm branch. This source search does not prove every indirect base/provider behavior, and does not prove that normal sleep necessarily triggers NotResponding.

The current IOUSBHost binding caches physical service termination and ignores nontermination interest messages. It has no dedicated original enterSleep/awakeFromSleep lifetime/anchor invalidation path if existing IO remains active. A real host StopIO/StartIO sequence resets/drains ISO/rings/anchors and may be the necessary modern sleep binding, but that substitution is physically UNVERIFIED. If the host does not stop/restart IO, explicit original wake wire-clear and clock-reset behavior is not currently mapped. Preserve this as a power-binding validation/compatibility question. Do not equate a powered-on notification with permission to replay commands, reset USB generation or rearm a suspended EP1 reader.
